title: Move delta_stack into TreeDecodeBufs for allocation reuse
description:
## Task: Move delta_stack into TreeDecodeBufs for allocation reuse

**File:** src/git_scan/object_store.rs:289-327, 620
**Severity:** P3 — per-call heap allocation on hot path
**Found by:** Architecture review during PR #98 review

### Problem

In read_pack_object (line 620), delta_stack is allocated as Vec::new() on every call:

    let mut delta_stack: Vec<TreeDeltaFrame> = Vec::new();

For the tree-loading path during commit-history diffing, read_pack_object is called once per delta-encoded tree object. With thousands of delta chains in a large repo, this generates allocation pressure.

The blob execution path already avoids this by embedding delta_stack in DecodeBufs (pack_exec.rs:883). The tree path should be consistent.

### Steps

1. Add delta_stack: Vec<TreeDeltaFrame> to TreeDecodeBufs struct (object_store.rs:289)

2. In TreeDecodeBufs::new(), initialize delta_stack: Vec::new()

3. In read_pack_object, replace the local Vec::new() with self.decode_bufs.delta_stack.clear() at the top, then use self.decode_bufs.delta_stack throughout Phase 1

4. Ensure Phase 2 iteration still works (it iterates delta_stack.iter().rev() — this should work on a field reference just as well as a local)

5. Verify the buffer is properly cleared between calls

### Files touched
- src/git_scan/object_store.rs (lines 289-327 struct, line 620 usage)

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] delta_stack is a field of TreeDecodeBufs
- [ ] No per-call Vec::new() allocation in read_pack_object
- [ ] delta_stack is cleared at the start of each read_pack_object call
- [ ] Structural parity with DecodeBufs in pack_exec.rs
- [ ] cargo test --all-features passes
close_reason: WRONG: delta_stack must remain local in read_pack_object due to REF delta re-entrancy. load_object_with_depth at line 751 re-enters read_pack_object, which would clobber a shared delta_stack. See scratch-faqz for the correct analysis. Moving it to TreeDecodeBufs would introduce use-after-free.

title: Document pointer stability invariant for apply_delta
description:
Security audit recommendation: the apply_delta function in pack_inflate.rs captures `out_ptr = out.as_mut_ptr()` after clear+reserve, then uses it throughout the loop. The critical invariant is that NO Vec operation occurs between the pointer capture and the final set_len — otherwise reallocation would invalidate the pointer.

This invariant is implicit and could be broken by a future maintainer adding an `out.push()`, `out.extend()`, or `out.reserve()` inside the loop.

Steps:
1. Add a prominent SAFETY comment block above the `let out_ptr = out.as_mut_ptr();` line (pack_inflate.rs ~line 677) explaining:
   - The pointer is valid because reserve(result_size) pre-allocates all needed capacity
   - NO Vec methods may be called on `out` between this line and `set_len(written)`
   - Adding push/extend/reserve here would invalidate out_ptr → use-after-free
   - The loop uses ONLY raw pointer writes via copy_nonoverlapping
2. cargo check to verify.

File: src/git_scan/pack_inflate.rs (line ~677)
close_reason: Added SAFETY pointer stability comment above out_ptr capture

title: Replace BFS exec_order with cache-aware DFS subtree-contiguous ordering
description:
## Problem

`build_exec_order` in `src/git_scan/pack_plan.rs:624` uses Kahn's algorithm with
a BTreeSet ready queue, producing BFS-like topological ordering. This maximizes
cache frontier width: all roots are processed before any depth-1 node, forcing
all base objects to survive simultaneously in PackCache until dependents arrive.

When a base is evicted before its last dependent, `decode_base_from_pack` must
re-walk the entire delta chain (re-parse headers, re-inflate, re-apply deltas).
This fallback is tracked by `base_cache_misses` and `fallback_base_decodes`.

## Research

### Git C (index-pack.c) — battle-tested approach
Uses LIFO work stack with `children_remaining` counter per base. Processes
base then ALL its children recursively before next base. Prunes cache when
counter hits zero. This is DFS subtree-contiguous ordering.

### Pebbling game theory (Blocki & Zhou 2016)
The "given a DAG, find processing order minimizing peak cached entries" problem
is the black pebbling game. NP-hard for general DAGs, but for TREES (which
delta chains predominantly are — each delta has exactly one base), postorder
DFS is provably optimal for minimizing peak pebble count.

### Elimination tree ordering (sparse matrix literature)
Postorder traversal of dependency tree minimizes cache working set. Used in
sparse Cholesky factorization — structurally identical to delta chain resolution.

### Graph reordering (Coleman et al.)
Grouping commonly-accessed nodes together yields up to 40% query time improvement.

## Solution

Replace BFS with DFS subtree-contiguous ordering in `build_exec_order`.
Four O(V+E) phases:

1. **Adjacency**: Build edges (base→dependents), indegree. Trigger on ANY delta
   deps (not just forward deps) — backward deps also benefit from contiguity.

2. **Descendant counts**: Reverse BFS from leaves, propagate desc_count upward.
   Exact for trees; over-counts for DAGs (acceptable tie-break heuristic).

3. **DFS with LIFO stack**: Sort children by ascending desc_count (thin subtrees
   first — they complete quickly, aging under CLOCK). Push roots sorted by
   descending desc_count. Push children only when dag_remaining hits zero
   (preserves topo invariant for DAGs).

4. **Validation**: Cycle check. Return None if result matches natural [0..n].

### Why thin-subtrees-first
Thin chains complete quickly and their cache entries age under CLOCK, becoming
evictable before the large subtree starts. Gives the large subtree effectively
more cache capacity.

### Why trigger on all deps (not just forward)
Consider offsets [10, 20, 50] where 20 and 50 both depend on base 10.
Natural ascending: 10, 20, 50 — base 10 survives 2 intervening offsets.
DFS contiguous: 10, 20, 50 — immediate reuse, 0 intervening offsets.
Improvement compounds with interleaved independent chains.

## Files to modify

- `src/git_scan/pack_plan.rs` — rewrite `build_exec_order` (lines 624-697), add unit tests
- `src/git_scan/pack_plan_model.rs` — add `delta_tree_roots` and `delta_tree_max_depth` to PackPlanStats

Files that should NOT change: pack_exec.rs, pack_cache.rs, runner_exec.rs.
The executor already consumes exec_order: Option<Vec<u32>> generically.

## Unit tests to add

- dfs_groups_subtrees_contiguously: Fan-out tree, verify contiguous subtrees
- dfs_thin_subtree_first: Verify thin child processed before fat child
- dfs_linear_chain: 10→20→30→40, verify sequential output
- dfs_dag_shared_base: Node with two parents, verify valid topo order
- dfs_returns_none_no_deps: No delta deps → None
- dfs_returns_none_natural_order: Result matches [0..n] → None
- dfs_cycle_detected: Verify cycle detection error

## Verification

1. cargo test -p scanner-rs — all existing + new tests pass
2. cargo test --test integration — pack exec integration tests pass
3. Benchmark: compare base_cache_hits/(hits+misses), fallback_base_decodes,
   fallback_resolve_nanos, and wall time before/after on real repos
notes:
CONSTRAINT: Diagnostic stats (delta_tree_roots, delta_tree_max_depth) must be
populated via perf_stats helpers, which compile to no-ops without the perf-stats
feature flag. Fields exist in struct unconditionally (zeroed by Default), but
mutations use perf_stats::set_u32() gated behind
#[cfg(all(feature = "perf-stats", debug_assertions))].

A set_u32 helper needs to be added to src/perf_stats.rs (currently only has
set_u64 and set_usize).

The DFS algorithm itself is NOT behind a feature flag — it replaces BFS
unconditionally. Only the diagnostic counters are gated.

title: Charge discarded bytes after budget clamp in read loops
description:
## Problem

When charge_decompressed_out(n) clamps to allowed < n, the n - allowed bytes were decompressed but never charged to archive/root counters. These phantom bytes undercount actual decompression work by up to 256 KB per clamp event (one ARCHIVE_STREAM_READ_MAX buffer).

## Why This Matters

The phantom bytes problem is well-documented in streaming decompression systems. The pre-charge + clamp pattern in budget.rs (lines 413-428) correctly caps the buffer size before each read via remaining_decompressed_allowance_with_ratio_probe(), but the decoder may still produce more output than requested because DEFLATE operates on indivisible compressed blocks internally. When the caller receives n bytes but the budget only allows allowed < n, the difference is silently dropped.

Reference: The existing charge_discarded_out() function (budget.rs:499-566) already handles this exact scenario — it bypasses per-entry caps but enforces archive/root/ratio caps. It exists specifically for bytes that were read but not delivered. The gap is that the three read loops don't call it after a clamp event.

## Files to Modify

- src/archive/scan.rs ~line 593-594 (gzip loop): Add charge_discarded_out() after clamp-and-break
- src/archive/scan.rs ~line 1170 (tar loop): Same pattern
- src/archive/scan.rs ~line 1573 (zip loop): Same pattern

## Implementation Guide

In each of the three read loops, after the existing clamp logic:

```rust
// EXISTING (gzip loop, ~line 582-594):
let charge = budgets.charge_decompressed_out(n as u64);
let allowed_usize = match charge {
    ChargeResult::Ok => n,
    ChargeResult::Clamp { allowed, hit } => {
        entry_partial_reason = Some(budget_hit_to_partial(hit, PartialReason::GzipCorrupt));
        allowed as usize
    }
};

// ADD after the Clamp arm, before break:
if allowed_usize < n {
    let discarded = (n as u64).saturating_sub(allowed_usize as u64);
    let _ = budgets.charge_discarded_out(discarded);
}
```

Key detail: charge_discarded_out() returns a ChargeResult but we ignore it (let _ =) because we're already breaking out of the loop. The important effect is updating the archive/root counters.

Existing code reference: charge_discarded_out() at budget.rs:499-566 already skips per-entry caps (line 520-526: only checks rem_arch, rem_root, rem_ratio). This is correct — the entry is being terminated, so per-entry accounting is irrelevant.

## Three Loop Locations (exact patterns)

Gzip loop (scan.rs ~line 582-617):
- Read at line 566-573: n = gz.read(dst)
- Charge at line 582: budgets.charge_decompressed_out(n as u64)
- Clamp handling at line 586-594
- Insert discard charge after line 594, before the break or next iteration

Tar loop (scan.rs ~line 1163-1202):
- Read at line 1148: n = reader.read(dst)
- Charge at line 1163: budgets.charge_decompressed_out(n as u64)
- Clamp handling at line 1167-1175
- Insert discard charge after line 1175

Zip loop (scan.rs ~line 1566-1602):
- Read at line 1545: n = reader.read_decompressed(dst)
- Charge at line 1566: budgets.charge_decompressed_out(n as u64)
- Clamp handling at line 1570-1578
- Insert discard charge after line 1578

## Tests

1. Unit test: Compress 100B payload, set per-entry cap to 50B. After scan, verify frame.decompressed_out at archive level accounts for all bytes (should be >= 50, reflecting the clamped delivery plus the discarded overshoot).
2. Property test (proptest): Generate random (budget, read_sizes) pairs. After all charges + discards, verify archive_decompressed_out + archive_discarded_out >= sum(all_reads).

## Verification

cargo fmt --all && cargo check && cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
cargo test -p scanner-rs --lib archive

## Estimate: ~30 LOC

title: Add confidence levels to rules
description:
## Problem
All 223 rules are loaded unconditionally. Generic rules (generic-api-key, jwt-base64, private-key) match extremely broadly and account for the majority of FPs. Kingfisher tags these as confidence: low and excludes them by default. This is the single biggest lever — potentially eliminating 60-70% of findings.

## Dependencies
None. Independent. Can proceed in parallel with Tasks scratch-ev8e and scratch-qric.

## Files to Modify

### src/api.rs (~line 30)
Add Confidence enum:
```rust
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash)]
pub enum Confidence {
    Low = 0,
    #[default]
    Medium = 1,
    High = 2,
}

impl Confidence {
    pub fn is_at_least(self, threshold: Confidence) -> bool {
        self >= threshold
    }
}
```
Using PartialOrd/Ord derive with discriminant ordering avoids manual match arms. Add serde Serialize/Deserialize if RuleSpec derives them. Check existing derives on RuleSpec to match.

### src/api.rs:563 (RuleSpec struct)
Add field: pub confidence: Confidence
Make sure to add #[serde(default)] so existing rules without the field default to Medium.

### src/api.rs (~line 1004, Tuning struct)
Add field: pub min_confidence: Confidence
Default should be Medium (via #[serde(default)]). This means Low-confidence rules are excluded by default.

### src/rules/yaml.rs:57-98 (YamlRule struct)
Add field: confidence: Option<String> with #[serde(default)]

### src/rules/yaml.rs:326-413 (parse function)
Parse the confidence string to enum:
```rust
let confidence = match yaml_rule.confidence.as_deref() {
    Some("low") => Confidence::Low,
    Some("high") => Confidence::High,
    Some("medium") | None => Confidence::Medium,
    Some(other) => return Err(format!("unknown confidence level: {other}")),
};
```
Add confidence field to the RuleSpec construction.

### src/engine/core.rs (~line 426, Engine::new or new_with_anchor_policy)
Filter rules below min_confidence before the compilation loop:
```rust
let rules: Vec<RuleSpec> = rules
    .into_iter()
    .filter(|r| r.confidence.is_at_least(tuning.min_confidence))
    .collect();
```
This must happen BEFORE rules are assigned rule_id indices and compiled. Check the exact location where rules are iterated for compilation and insert the filter there.

### default_rules.yaml
Tag specific rules:
- confidence: low → generic-api-key, jwt-base64, private-key (3 rules)
- confidence: high → Rules with offline_validation (checksum/structural validation): aws-access-token, github-pat, github-fine-grained-pat, and any others with offline_validation specs
- All other rules: No field needed (defaults to Medium via serde(default))

### docs/data-types.md
Add Confidence to RuleSpec and Tuning class diagrams.

### docs/detection-rules.md
Add Confidence section explaining the low/medium/high levels, and update the YAML template to show the confidence field.

## Testing
1. Unit test: two rules (Low + High), Engine with min_confidence: Medium → only High compiled. Verify the Low rule is not in the compiled set.
2. YAML round-trip test with confidence field present and absent.
3. cargo test --all — builtin_rules_count test may need adjustment if it counts compiled rules and min_confidence filtering applies. Check whether the test creates its own Engine with specific tuning or uses defaults.
4. Verify demo_tuning() sets min_confidence: Medium (check src/api.rs for the demo_tuning function).

## Performance
Large positive. Excluding low-confidence rules at load time shrinks the Vectorscan prefilter DB, reduces anchor hits, and eliminates all downstream work for those rules.

## Validation
cargo fmt --all && cargo check && cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings

title: Add zstd decompression support (.tar.zst, .zst)
description:
## Context

Zstandard (.zst, .tar.zst) is growing rapidly in package ecosystems (Arch Linux packages, Fedora RPMs, cargo crates, modern tarballs). The zstd crate wraps the C reference implementation. CRITICAL safety requirement: window_log_max(25) MUST be set to prevent the 3.75TB window allocation attack (RUSTSEC-2024-0400 documented memory safety bugs in pure-Rust ruzstd; C binding is safer).

Evidence: Phase 3 Deep-Dive 2 (P3.2.F1): zstd default window can be 3.75TB, window_log_max(25) caps at 32MB. Phase 4 Contrarian (P4.4.F1): facebook/zstd#3638 documents production OOM from large windows. RUSTSEC-2024-0400: memory safety bugs in ruzstd. Phase 1 Agent 7 (P1.7.F1): decompression at 1347 MB/s (2.6x faster than gzip).

## Current State

- .zst is in path policy skip set (src/git_scan/path_policy.rs — packed extension b"zst")
- No zstd dependency in Cargo.toml
- ArchiveKind has no zstd variant
- zstd magic bytes: 0x28, 0xB5, 0x2F, 0xFD (4 bytes)

## Desired State

- New ArchiveKind::Zstd and ArchiveKind::TarZstd variants
- New src/archive/formats/zstd.rs module with ZstdStream<R>
- Extension detection: .zst → Zstd, .tar.zst → TarZstd
- Magic detection: 0x28 0xB5 0x2F 0xFD → Zstd
- window_log_max(25) enforced at construction (32MB max window)
- .zst REMOVED from path policy skip set
- Budget integration via CountedRead
- Simulation harness and corpus tests for zstd format

## Implementation Guidance

### Dependency:
Add to Cargo.toml: `zstd = "0.13"` (C binding, stable API, supports window_log_max)

### Files to modify:
Same dispatch-site checklist as bzip2 task, plus:
1. `src/archive/detect.rs` — Add Zstd/TarZstd variants; extension detection for last byte b"t" (.zst ends in t); magic sniffing for 4-byte zstd signature
2. `src/archive/formats/zstd.rs` (new) — ZstdStream<R> with MANDATORY window_log_max(25)
3. All dispatch sites (same list as bzip2 task: scan.rs, local_fs_archive_ctx.rs, local_fs_uring.rs, local_fs_tar.rs, sim_scanner)
4. `src/scheduler/local_fs_zstd.rs` (new) — mirrors local_fs_gzip.rs
5. `src/git_scan/path_policy.rs` — Remove zst from SKIP_EXTS
6. `src/sim_archive/build_zstd.rs` (new) — Deterministic zstd archive builder for sim harness
7. `src/sim_archive/mod.rs` — Export build_zstd_bytes

### ZstdStream pattern:
```rust
pub struct ZstdStream<R: Read> {
    dec: zstd::Decoder<'static, CountedRead<R>>,
    last_bytes: u64,
}
impl<R: Read> ZstdStream<R> {
    pub fn new(reader: R) -> io::Result<Self> {
        let counted = CountedRead::new(reader);
        let mut dec = zstd::Decoder::new(counted)?;
        dec.window_log_max(25)?;  // CRITICAL: cap at 32MB
        Ok(Self { dec, last_bytes: 0 })
    }
}
```

### Key difference from bzip2:
- zstd Decoder::new is FALLIBLE (returns Result) unlike flate2 which is infallible
- Must handle construction error by mapping to ArchiveEnd::Skipped(IoError)
- C dependency (unlike bzip2 pure Rust) — requires C compiler, but this is already the case due to flate2 zlib-ng and vectorscan-rs-sys

### Extension detection:
.zst ends in "t". No existing extensions dispatch on b"t". Add `b't' => detect_t_suffix(name, len)` to the main match. detect_t_suffix checks .zst (4 chars), .tar.zst (8 chars).

### Magic detection:
0x28 0xB5 0x2F 0xFD (4 bytes). Distinct first byte 0x28 — no collision with existing formats.

## Simulation Harness Testing

The archive simulation harness provides deterministic end-to-end testing through the full scanner pipeline. New decompression formats MUST be wired into the sim harness.

### Required sim harness additions:

1. **Add `Zstd` / `TarZstd` to `ArchiveKindSpec`** (src/sim_scanner/scenario.rs).
2. **Add `build_zstd_bytes`** (src/sim_archive/build_zstd.rs) — deterministic zstd archive materializer. Compresses payload with `zstd::stream::write::Encoder`, returns bytes.
3. **Wire materialization** in `src/sim_archive/mod.rs` `materialize_archive()` match arms.
4. **Wire sim runner dispatch** in `src/sim_scanner/runner.rs` `ArchiveScanState::step()` match arms.
5. **Add to generator** in `src/sim_scanner/generator.rs` so random scenarios include zstd archives.

### Required sim corpus tests (tests/simulation/scanner_archive_corpus.rs):

Follow the existing wall-clock timeout tests as templates:

```rust
// Smoke: zstd archive with secret is scanned
#[test]
fn archive_zstd_smoke() { ... }

// Budget: per-entry byte cap limits zstd scan
#[test]
fn archive_zstd_entry_byte_cap() { ... }

// Memory safety: window_log_max(25) prevents OOM
#[test]
fn archive_zstd_large_window_rejected() { ... }

// Wall-clock timeout via countdown
#[test]
fn archive_zstd_wall_clock_timeout_skips_later_entries() {
    // Same pattern as tar/zip/targz timeout tests
    run_archive_scenario_with_countdown(scenario, archive_cfg, seed, 2);
}
```

### Deterministic deadline testing with countdown:

`RunConfig.archive_deadline_countdown` (gated by `#[cfg(any(test, feature = "sim-harness"))]`) arms a deterministic countdown in `ArchiveBudgets`. Each call to `is_deadline_expired()` decrements the counter; when it hits 0 the method returns `true` without consulting the real clock. Use `run_archive_scenario_with_countdown(scenario, cfg, seed, N)` where N is the number of allowed checks before firing.

## Code References

```rust
// src/archive/formats/gzip.rs:101-182 — GzipStream template
// src/archive/detect.rs:170-184 — detect_kind_from_name_bytes
// src/archive/detect.rs:118-129 — sniff_kind_from_header
// src/sim_archive/build_gzip.rs — gzip materializer (template for build_zstd.rs)
// tests/simulation/scanner_archive_corpus.rs:860-990 — wall-clock timeout corpus test patterns
// zstd crate API: zstd::stream::read::Decoder, window_log_max()
```

## Related Work

- scratch-bqm3: parent epic
- scratch-m1om: wall-clock timeout (prerequisite, now implemented)
- scratch-gasn: bzip2 decompression task (establishes the new-format pattern; review sequentially)

## Acceptance Criteria

- cargo fmt --all && cargo check && cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings passes

- cargo test --features sim-harness --test simulation passes (including new zstd corpus tests)
- ZstdStream::new() sets window_log_max(25) — verified by unit test
- Unit test: decompressing a stream requiring window > 32MB returns an error (not OOM)
- .zst files are no longer skipped by path policy
- detect_kind_from_name_bytes(b"file.tar.zst") returns Some(ArchiveKind::TarZstd)
- sniff_kind_from_header with zstd magic returns Some(ArchiveKind::Zstd)
- Secrets inside .tar.zst archives are found (smoke test)

title: Use checked arithmetic for delta insert pos+size in pack_inflate
description:
## Task: Use checked arithmetic for delta insert pos+size in pack_inflate

**File:** src/git_scan/pack_inflate.rs:707
**Severity:** P3 — style inconsistency, not a correctness issue
**Found by:** Unsafe code safety audit during PR #98 review

### Problem

Line 707 in apply_delta_into uses plain addition for bounds checking:

    if pos + size > delta.len() {

While this cannot overflow in practice (size is a u8 with bit 7 clear, so size ∈ [1, 127]), it's inconsistent with the defensive arithmetic style used elsewhere in the same function:
- Line 686: off.checked_add(size) for copy offset
- Line 693: written.saturating_add(size) for result bounds
- Line 710: written.saturating_add(size) for insert bounds
- Line 827: start.checked_add(needed) in decode_copy_params

### Steps

1. Change line 707 from:
   ```rust
   if pos + size > delta.len() {
   ```
   to:
   ```rust
   if delta.len() - pos < size {
   ```
   or:
   ```rust
   if pos.saturating_add(size) > delta.len() {
   ```

2. Verify no behavior change with existing tests

### Files touched
- src/git_scan/pack_inflate.rs (line 707, one-line change)

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Arithmetic is consistent with defensive style used in surrounding code
- [ ] No functional change
- [ ] cargo test --all-features passes

## Bug: Fix misleading SplitMix64 comment in tree_cache hash

**File:** src/git_scan/tree_cache.rs:278-292
**Severity:** P3 — misleading documentation, not a correctness issue
**Found by:** Pattern recognition review during PR #98 review

### Problem

The hash_oid function comment says "SplitMix64 avalanche" but the implementation uses Murmur3 fmix64 constants:

    h = h.wrapping_mul(0xff51afd7ed558ccd);  // Murmur3 constant

The real SplitMix64 finalizer (Stafford variant 13) uses different constants:
    0xbf58476d1ce4e5b9 and 0x94d049bb133111eb

The correct implementation IS used in blob_introducer.rs:811-817 (mix64 function), correctly labeled "Stafford variant 13 bit mixer."

Also in tree_delta_cache.rs:349-355, the same Murmur3 fmix is used with the same misleading comment.

The single-round Murmur3 fmix is perfectly adequate for cache set indexing — this is purely a comment accuracy issue.

### Steps

1. **Write a test first** that documents the expected hash behavior:
   - Test that hash_oid produces consistent output for known inputs (pin the current behavior)
   - This ensures the fix is comment-only and doesn't accidentally change the hash function

2. Update comment in tree_cache.rs:278 from "SplitMix64 avalanche" to "Murmur3 fmix64 finalizer"

3. Update the same comment in tree_delta_cache.rs:349 if it exists there too

4. No functional code changes — the hash function itself is fine for its purpose

title: Add min_confidence to RuleCold and auto-compute defaults
description:
## Context
After schema support (`scratch-nqqy`), engine compilation still needs to carry a final per-rule threshold into runtime validation. `RuleCold` currently stores only `name`, so there is nowhere to hold effective `min_confidence` at scan time.

Primary references:
- `src/engine/rule_repr.rs` (`RuleCold` definition)
- `src/engine/core.rs` (rule compilation loop and `rules_cold.push(...)`)
- `src/api.rs` (`confidence::*` constants)

## Goal
Extend `RuleCold` with `min_confidence: i8` and compute the final runtime threshold during engine build from either explicit YAML override or auto-default policy derived from compiled gate metadata.

## Required Code Changes
### 1) Extend cold metadata
File: `src/engine/rule_repr.rs`
- Update `RuleCold`:
```rust
pub(super) struct RuleCold {
    pub(super) name: &'static str,
    pub(super) min_confidence: i8,
}
```

### 2) Add defaulting policy in engine build
File: `src/engine/core.rs`
- In the rule compile loop (currently around `let (mut rule, gates) = compile_rule(spec);`), compute effective threshold:
  - explicit override wins: `spec.min_confidence.unwrap_or_else(...)`
  - otherwise use auto-default policy from compiled metadata.

Use this exact auto-default policy (Phase 1):
1. If rule has offline validation gate -> default `5` (`confidence::OFFLINE_VALID`).
2. Else if rule has both keyword and entropy gates -> default `3` (`KEYWORD_PRESENT + ENTROPY_PASS`).
3. Else if rule has assignment-shape check -> default `2` (`ASSIGNMENT_SHAPE`).
4. Else -> default `0` (no confidence filtering).

Rationale: only assign non-zero defaults where confidence signals are strong enough to be intentional FP filters.

- Store result in `rules_cold.push(RuleCold { ... })`.

### 3) Add accessor for runtime use
File: `src/engine/core.rs`
- Add a small helper used by gate resolution:
```rust
#[inline(always)]
pub(super) fn rule_min_confidence(&self, rule_id: u32) -> i8 {
    self.rules_cold[rule_id as usize].min_confidence
}
```

## Tests
File targets:
- `src/engine/tests.rs`

Add tests covering:
- explicit override precedence (`min_confidence: Some(7)` -> effective 7 even if auto policy would differ).
- offline-validation rule auto-defaults to 5.
- keywords+entropy rule auto-defaults to 3.
- assignment-shape-only rule auto-defaults to 2.
- plain rule defaults to 0.

## Reference Snippet
Current cold metadata push site:
```rust
// src/engine/core.rs
rules_cold.push(RuleCold { name: spec.name });
```

## Verification
```bash
cargo fmt --all
cargo check
cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
cargo test src/engine/tests.rs
```

## Acceptance Criteria
- `RuleCold` contains `min_confidence` and remains parallel to `rules_hot`.
- Effective threshold uses explicit override first, then the defined auto-default policy.
- Runtime accessor exists for window validation.
- Engine tests verify policy branches and override precedence.
close_reason: All requirements verified: RuleCold has min_confidence field, derive_min_confidence computes auto-defaults, accessor exists, 16 tests pass covering all policy branches and override precedence.

title: Add wall-clock timeout to archive budget system
description:
## Context

The existing archive budget system (ArchiveBudgets) is purely byte/count-based with no CPU-time defense. Adding new decompression formats (especially bzip2 at ~40 MB/s) widens the CPU-exhaustion attack surface. A crafted archive can exhaust CPU within byte budgets. This must be addressed before shipping new decompressors.

Evidence: Phase 4 adversarial review identified this as the strongest challenge (75% confidence). The budget system at src/archive/budget.rs:5-6 explicitly states "no wall-clock timeouts" as a design principle. The inflation ratio check at budget.rs:448-451 has a bootstrap gap when comp_in=0.

## Current State

- `ArchiveConfig` (src/archive/config.rs:48-79) has byte/count/ratio limits only
- `ArchiveBudgets` (src/archive/budget.rs:1-6) explicitly avoids wall-clock timeouts
- Scan loops in src/archive/scan.rs check budgets after each read() but have no time guard
- Scheduler loops in src/scheduler/local_fs_archive_ctx.rs, local_fs_gzip.rs, local_fs_tar.rs, local_fs_zip.rs similarly have no time bounds

## Desired State

- `ArchiveConfig` gains `max_wall_clock_per_archive: Option<Duration>` (default Some(30s))
- Lightweight `Deadline` type wraps `Option<Instant>` with `#[inline(always)] fn is_expired(&self) -> bool`
- Each archive scan entry point creates a Deadline from config at scan start
- Inner read loops check deadline.is_expired() after each chunk read (amortized, not per-byte)
- Timeout produces `ArchiveEnd::Partial(PartialReason::WallClockTimeout)`
- Simulation tests are NOT affected (deadline is None in sim mode, preserving determinism)

## Implementation Guidance

### Files to modify:
1. `src/archive/outcome.rs` — Add `PartialReason::WallClockTimeout` variant, update COUNT, PARTIAL_REASONS array, name() match
2. `src/archive/config.rs` — Add `pub max_wall_clock_per_archive: Option<Duration>` to ArchiveConfig
3. `src/archive/budget.rs` — Add `Deadline` type (Option<Instant> wrapper)
4. `src/archive/scan.rs` — Thread Deadline through scan functions, add is_expired() check after each chunk read
5. `src/scheduler/local_fs_gzip.rs`, `local_fs_tar.rs`, `local_fs_zip.rs` — Same deadline checks
6. `src/sim_scanner/runner.rs` — Set max_wall_clock_per_archive: None for simulation

### Patterns to follow:
- The existing ArchiveEnd::Partial(PartialReason::*) pattern for early termination
- The existing ArchiveConfig default impl pattern
- saturating arithmetic throughout (consistent with budget.rs conventions)

## Code References

```rust
// src/archive/config.rs:48-79 — ArchiveConfig struct
// src/archive/budget.rs:1-6 — "no wall-clock" design principle
// src/archive/budget.rs:448-451 — inflation ratio bootstrap gap
// src/archive/outcome.rs:193 — PartialReason enum
// src/archive/scan.rs:544-633 — gzip entry loop (template for deadline check placement)
```

## Related Work

- scratch-jktv: per-entry inflation ratio tracking (complementary budget hardening)
- scratch-iqoe: charge discarded bytes after budget clamp (budget correctness)
- scratch-viqx: config cross-validation for inflation ratio vs byte caps (budget validation)
- scratch-bqm3: parent epic (multi-format archive support)

## Acceptance Criteria

- cargo fmt --all && cargo check && cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings passes
- cargo test passes (existing budget tests unaffected)
- New unit test: config with Some(Duration::ZERO) immediately returns PartialReason::WallClockTimeout
- Simulation tests pass with deterministic behavior (no Instant dependency in sim)
- Wall-clock timeout measured at chunk-read granularity (not per-byte) to minimize syscall overhead

## Pointers

- src/archive/budget.rs for the full budget lifecycle (reset→enter→begin_entry→charge→end_entry→exit)
- src/archive/scan.rs:544-633 for the gzip scan loop structure (template for where deadline check goes)
- tests/integration/archive_scanning.rs for existing budget enforcement tests
- tests/simulation/scanner_budget_invariance.rs for sim framework integration

description:
## Task 9: Implement report output and regression verdict

**Priority:** P1 | **Type:** task | **Depends on:** Task 8 (metrics)

### Why
The harness must produce: machine-readable JSON (CI), human-readable table (terminal), diff report (regression investigation). The regression module compares metrics against stored baselines and emits BLOCK/WARN/PASS for CI gating.

### Files to Create
- `tools/eval-harness/src/report.rs`
- `tools/eval-harness/src/regression.rs`

### Files to Modify
- `tools/eval-harness/src/lib.rs` — add `pub mod report; pub mod regression;`

### Regression Thresholds
- BLOCK: PRC-AUC drops >5% OR any rule F1 drops >10%
- WARN: PRC-AUC drops 2-5% OR any rule F1 drops 5-10%
- PASS: All deltas below WARN thresholds

### Implementation — regression.rs

```rust
use crate::metrics::EvalMetrics;

#[derive(Debug, Clone, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct RegressionThresholds {
    pub max_prc_auc_drop_block: f64,   // 0.05 = 5%
    pub max_prc_auc_drop_warn: f64,    // 0.02 = 2%
}

impl Default for RegressionThresholds {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self { max_prc_auc_drop_block: 0.05, max_prc_auc_drop_warn: 0.02 }
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub enum Verdict { Pass, Warn, Block }

#[derive(Debug, Clone, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct RegressionVerdict {
    pub verdict: Verdict,
    pub message: Option<String>,
    pub prc_auc_delta: Option<f64>,
}

pub fn check_regression(
    current: &EvalMetrics,
    baseline: Option<&EvalMetrics>,
    thresholds: &RegressionThresholds,
) -> RegressionVerdict { /* ... */ }
```

### Implementation — report.rs

```rust
use crate::metrics::EvalMetrics;
use crate::regression::RegressionVerdict;

#[derive(Debug, serde::Serialize)]
pub struct EvalReport {
    pub corpus: String,

    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub regression: Option<RegressionVerdict>,
}

pub fn render_json(report: &EvalReport) -> String { /* ... */ }
pub fn render_table(report: &EvalReport) -> String { /* ... */ }
```

### Testing Strategy
- 9 unit tests for regression: pass when met, block when exceeded, exact boundary behavior, NaN always fails, one failing metric fails suite, all passing passes, no baseline -> pass
- 3 proptest: determinism, monotonicity of failure, NaN always fails

### Acceptance Criteria
1. render_json produces valid JSON that round-trips
2. render_table contains PRC-AUC, Precision, Recall, F1, per-rule rows
3. check_regression -> Pass when no baseline
4. check_regression -> Block when PRC-AUC drops >5%
5. check_regression -> Warn when drop is 2-5%
6. Exit code mapping: Pass/Warn -> 0, Block -> 1

### B. Error Book (Top FP/FN Analysis)

**Research basis:**
- Semgrep: Rule-first grouping maximizes actionability. [P1.8.F6, evidence 3]
- detect-secrets: audit --stats for per-plugin signal-to-noise. [P1.5.F6, evidence 3]
- TruffleHog: DefaultFalsePositives list + Aho-Corasick wordlist filtering. [P1.5.F4, evidence 3]
- detect-secrets: SHA-1 hash-before-persist. Secret never serialized. [P1.8.F1, evidence 3]
- CredData: Three-layer privacy — substitution, anonymization, metadata separation. [P1.8.F2, evidence 4]
- Gitleaks: Fingerprint = commit:path:rule:line. --redact percentage. [P1.8.F3, evidence 3]

**Implementation outline (in report.rs):**

    #[derive(Debug, Clone, serde::Serialize)]
    pub struct ErrorBookEntry {
        pub path: String,
        pub rule: String,
        pub confidence: i8,
        pub classification: String,    // "FP" or "FN"
        pub redacted_context: Option<String>,  // "[REDACTED:32]...text..."
        pub secret_hash: String,       // BLAKE3 keyed hash for dedup
    }

    #[derive(Debug, Clone, serde::Serialize)]
    pub struct ErrorBook {
        pub top_fps: Vec<ErrorBookEntry>,
        pub top_fns: Vec<ErrorBookEntry>,
        pub fp_by_rule: Vec<(String, u64)>,  // (rule, count) desc
        pub fn_by_rule: Vec<(String, u64)>,
    }

    fn build_error_book(classified, false_negatives, corpus_root, max_entries) -> ErrorBook
    // 1. Group FPs by rule, sort by count desc
    // 2. Take top max_entries, read context if corpus available
    // 3. Redact: replace secret span with [REDACTED:{len}]
    // 4. Hash: blake3::keyed_hash(key, secret_bytes) for dedup

    fn redact_context(file_content, match_start, match_end, context_chars) -> String
    // Return: before_text + [REDACTED:N] + after_text

Add to EvalReport:
    pub error_book: Option<ErrorBook>,

**Privacy:** BLAKE3 keyed hash (not plain SHA) prevents rainbow-table recovery of short API keys.

**Tests:**

- redact_context replaces exact span with [REDACTED:N]
- Empty corpus_root -> context is None, no panic

notes:
## Final Validation Results

### Quality Gates — All Pass
- `cargo fmt --all` — clean (no formatting issues)
- `cargo check` — clean (no compiler warnings)
- `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features` — clean (no lint warnings)
- `cargo test` — 1536 unit tests + 13 doc tests passed, 0 failures

### Functional Validation — 59 Offline-Validation Tests

**API layer (6 tests):** `offline_suppresses_on_invalid`, CRC32 boundary/panic tests,
`offline_validation_none_is_valid`, value suppressor tests.

**Validator unit tests (33 tests):** AWS access key (prefix, charset, A3T),
CRC32-base62 (valid/invalid checksum, too-short), GitHub PAT (valid, wrong prefix,
invalid checksum), Grafana (valid/invalid/too-short), Sentry (structure, prefix,
separator, payload chars, signature), hex/base62/base64 decode edge cases.

**Engine integration tests (4 key tests):**

| Test | Scenario | Result |
|------|----------|--------|
| `offline_validation_suppresses_invalid_root_finding` | Invalid CRC token at root | 0 findings (suppressed), `offline_suppressed == 1` |
| `offline_validation_keeps_valid_root_finding` | Valid CRC token at root | 1 finding retained, `offline_suppressed == 0` |
| `offline_validation_mixed_valid_invalid_and_no_gate` | Valid + invalid + no-gate rule | 2 findings (valid CRC + no-gate kept, invalid CRC suppressed) |
| `offline_validation_does_not_suppress_non_root_findings` | Invalid token via Base64 transform | Finding retained (non-root bypasses gate) |

**Rule YAML parsing tests (16 tests):** Parse/roundtrip for all 5 validator types,
missing-field rejection, unknown-type rejection.

### Performance — No Regression

**Per-validator microbenchmarks (bench/offline_validation):**

| Validator | Case | Latency | Throughput | vs Baseline |
|-----------|------|---------|------------|-------------|
| AWS | valid_akia | 17.6 ns | 1.06 GiB/s | +3% (noise) |
| AWS | valid_a3t | 18.0 ns | 1.04 GiB/s | within noise |
| AWS | invalid_charset | 2.25 ns | 8.28 GiB/s | within noise |
| AWS | invalid_prefix | 2.35 ns | 7.92 GiB/s | within noise |
| Sentry | valid_small | 49.7 ns | 1.40 GiB/s | within noise |
| Sentry | valid_large | 203 ns | 3.17 GiB/s | -23% (improved) |
| Sentry | invalid_prefix | 189 ns | 3.40 GiB/s | -26% (improved) |
| Sentry | invalid_char | 183 ns | 3.52 GiB/s | -31% (improved) |
| Sentry | oversized | 30.1 ns | 28.1 GiB/s | -6% (improved) |

Invalid tokens rejected in 2-30 ns (fast-path early exit). No regressions.

**Full-engine throughput (bench/scanner_throughput):**

| Workload | Throughput |
|----------|-----------|
| tier1 ceiling (random 4MB) | 9.18 GiB/s |
| tier1 ceiling (ascii 4MB) | 28.14 GiB/s |
| full_engine/random_bytes | 130 MiB/s |
| full_engine/clean_ascii | 388 MiB/s |
| full_engine/sparse_anchors | 384 MiB/s |
| full_engine/moderate_secrets | 390 MiB/s |
| full_engine/mixed_realistic | 1.25 GiB/s |

The `post_scan_filter` offline gate has zero overhead when the gate pool is empty
(early-exit on `self.offline_gates.is_empty()`). When gates are active, cost is
bounded to O(findings × per-validator-cost), which is sub-microsecond for typical
workloads.

### Edge-Case Risks & Follow-Ups
- Transform-derived (non-root) findings intentionally bypass offline validation
  because extracted spans are in transformed space, not root space. This is correct
  behavior but means base64-encoded invalid tokens will not be suppressed.
- The current gate set covers 5 validators (AWS, CRC32-base62, GitHub PAT, Grafana,
  Sentry). Additional validators can be added incrementally by extending the
  `OfflineValidationSpec` enum and the `validate()` dispatch.
- No rules currently produce `Indeterminate` verdicts; all validators are
  binary (Valid/Invalid). The Indeterminate path is tested via the "no gate" case
  (findings without gates are kept, equivalent to Indeterminate).

title: Add min_confidence field to RuleSpec and YAML parser
description:
## Context
We need schema-level support for per-rule confidence filtering. Today `RuleSpec` does not carry a `min_confidence` field, so neither YAML nor runtime compilation can represent this policy.

Primary reference points:
- `src/api.rs` (`RuleSpec`, `assert_valid`, `encode_policy`)
- `src/rules/yaml.rs` (`YamlRule`, `parse_yaml_rules` -> `rules.push(RuleSpec { ... })`)
- `src/rules/yaml_unit_tests.rs` (round-trip + unknown-field whitelist)

## Goal
Add `min_confidence: Option<i8>` to rule schema and YAML parsing so rules can explicitly set a threshold, while preserving backward compatibility for rules that omit it.

## Required Code Changes
### 1) Extend `RuleSpec`
File: `src/api.rs`
- Add field to `RuleSpec`:
```rust
pub min_confidence: Option<i8>,
```
Placement: alongside other optional gate-like rule settings (near `offline_validation` / `uuid_format_secret`).

- Add validation in `RuleSpec::assert_valid`:
  - If `Some(v)`, require `0 <= v <= 10` (current confidence model output range).
  - Panic message should name `min_confidence` and the valid range.

- Update policy hashing encoding in `RuleSpec::encode_policy`:
  - Add deterministic encoding for `Option<i8>` (presence byte + value).
  - Rationale: threshold changes detection behavior and must invalidate policy fingerprints.

### 2) Extend YAML schema and conversion
File: `src/rules/yaml.rs`
- Add field to `YamlRule`:
```rust
#[serde(default)]
pub min_confidence: Option<i8>,
```
- Wire through conversion in `parse_yaml_rules` when constructing `RuleSpec`.

### 3) Update parser/round-trip test scaffolding
File: `src/rules/yaml_unit_tests.rs`
- `rulespec_to_yaml`: include `min_confidence` in produced `YamlRule`.
- `assert_rules_equal`: compare `orig.min_confidence` vs `parsed.min_confidence`.
- `default_rules_yaml_has_no_unknown_fields`: add `"min_confidence"` to allowed `rule_fields` whitelist.

### 4) Add focused tests for new field
At minimum:
- parse explicit integer value (`min_confidence: 3`) -> `Some(3)`.
- absent or null value -> `None`.
- out-of-range values (`-1`, `11`) fail validation with clear message.

## Backward Compatibility Requirements
- Existing YAML without `min_confidence` must continue to parse.
- Existing code paths creating `RuleSpec` literals must compile by setting `min_confidence: None` where needed.
  - Use compiler errors + `rg -n "RuleSpec \{" src tests` to update literals.

## Reference Snippet
Current YAML -> RuleSpec conversion site:
```rust
// src/rules/yaml.rs
rules.push(RuleSpec {
    name,
    anchors,
    radius,
    ...
    offline_validation,
    uuid_format_secret,
    secret_group,
    re,
});
```

## Verification
```bash
cargo fmt --all
cargo check
cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
cargo test --test integration doc_consistency
cargo test -p eval-harness
```

## Acceptance Criteria
- `RuleSpec` and `YamlRule` both support `min_confidence: Option<i8>`.
- YAML parse/round-trip/unknown-field tests are updated and passing.
- `RuleSpec::assert_valid` enforces the allowed range.
- Policy-hash encoding includes `min_confidence`.
- Build is green after all affected `RuleSpec` literals are updated.

title: Investigate software prefetch for scattered base copies
description:
## Summary

Investigation-only task. Measure L1D cache miss rate for scattered copy operations in delta chain decoding. Only add software prefetch hints if miss rate exceeds 5% on scattered access patterns.

## Context

Perf analysis (tools/bench-compare/results/perf_analysis.md) shows 0.982% L1D miss rate and 40.67% backend stalls on Graviton3. The backend stalls are memory-bandwidth bound, but the low L1D miss rate suggests the current access patterns are mostly sequential and cache-friendly.

Delta copy instructions can reference arbitrary offsets in the base object. For small base objects, the entire base fits in L1 cache. For large base objects with scattered copy offsets, prefetching the next copy's base region while processing the current copy could hide memory latency.

## Investigation Steps

1. **Create scattered-copy benchmark**: Generate synthetic delta instructions that copy from widely separated regions of a large (>256KB) base object, defeating L1 cache (typically 32-64KB on aarch64)
2. **Measure baseline L1D miss rate**: Run `perf stat -e L1-dcache-load-misses,L1-dcache-loads` on the scattered-copy benchmark
3. **Compare with sequential benchmark**: Same total copy volume but sequential base offsets (control case)
4. **If miss rate > 5%**: Prototype `std::arch::aarch64::_prefetch` (or `core::arch::x86_64::_mm_prefetch` on x86) with prefetch distance of 1 copy instruction ahead
5. **Measure improvement**: Compare throughput with and without prefetch on scattered benchmark

## Technical Notes

- On aarch64 (Graviton3): Use `PRFM PLDL1KEEP` via intrinsic, prefetch distance ~1-2 cache lines ahead of next copy source
- On x86_64: Use `_mm_prefetch` with `_MM_HINT_T0`
- Prefetch is only beneficial when: (a) access is scattered (not sequential), (b) base object exceeds L1 size, (c) copy count is high enough to amortize mispredicted prefetches
- The 0.982% overall L1D miss rate suggests this optimization has limited scope — it would only help for specific large-object scattered-copy workloads

## Decision Criteria

- If scattered-copy L1D miss rate > 5%: implement prefetch with conditional compilation (`#[cfg(target_arch)]`)
- If scattered-copy L1D miss rate ≤ 5%: close as "not actionable" with documented measurements
- If prefetch improves scattered-copy throughput < 3%: close as "not worth the complexity"

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Scattered-copy benchmark created and documented
- [ ] L1D miss rate measured for both scattered and sequential patterns
- [ ] Decision documented with measurements
- [ ] If implementing: prefetch works on both aarch64 and x86_64 via conditional compilation

title: Fix wrapping timestamp parse 20-digit overflow
description:
In commit_parse.rs:329, the length check `bytes.len() > 20` allows 20-digit inputs that can overflow u64 (max ~1.8e19, but 20 digits represent up to ~1e20). With wrapping_mul/wrapping_add, the overflow silently wraps. The comment at lines 346-352 is self-contradictory and acknowledges this.

In practice this is unreachable — the caller rejects timestamps > 32_503_680_000 (11 digits) — but the fix is trivial and eliminates a theoretical correctness gap.

Steps:
1. Add a failing test: construct a 20-digit decimal string that wraps to a value within the caller's accepted range [0, 32_503_680_000]. Verify parse_unix_timestamp currently returns Ok (the bug). The test should assert Err.
2. Change `bytes.len() > 20` to `bytes.len() > 19` in parse_unix_timestamp (19 digits max is 9_999_999_999_999_999_999 < u64::MAX, so wrapping is impossible).
3. Fix the self-contradictory comment block at lines 346-352 to accurately describe the safety argument.
4. Verify the new test passes and all existing tests still pass.

File: src/git_scan/commit_parse.rs
close_reason: Duplicate of scratch-xnon which has more comprehensive security analysis and TDD steps. scratch-xnon recommends >11 digits (tighter bound matching caller's year-3000 check) vs this issue's >19.

title: Extract sliding-window read loop helper for archive scanning
description:
The code review identified that the sliding-window read loop pattern is triplicated across the three archive format handlers in src/archive/scan.rs. Each format (gzip, tar, zip) has its own copy of the overlap-carry + read-fill + sink-deliver loop.

**Locations:**
- Gzip scan loop: src/archive/scan.rs (search for the gzip arm in scan_archive_impl)
- Tar scan loop: src/archive/scan.rs (tar arm)
- Zip scan loop: src/archive/scan.rs (zip arm)

The loops share the same structure:
1. Carry overlap bytes from end of previous chunk to start of buffer
2. Read new data into remaining buffer space via format-specific reader
3. Deliver chunk to sink via on_entry_chunk
4. Charge budget
5. Loop until EOF or budget hit

**Considerations:**
- The review noted this duplication may be intentional ('strategic') since each format has slightly different reader types and error handling
- A generic helper parameterized over the reader type (or using the TarRead trait) could unify the loop body
- Alternatively, a macro could stamp out the variants
- This is lower priority since the duplication is self-contained within one file and the loops are performance-critical hot paths where abstraction overhead should be zero-cost

title: Safelist against secret bytes not just context
description:
## Problem
suppress_root_finding_by_safelist (core.rs lines ~1109-1151) runs the 18-pattern SafelistFilter RegexSet only on context_buf[root_hint_start..root_hint_end] — the full match range in the context buffer. It never checks the extracted secret bytes. If the secret itself is hunter2, 0123456789, or ZXhhbXBsZQ== (base64 for "example") but the surrounding context is clean, the finding passes.

Kingfisher's is_safe_match() runs on the captured secret bytes directly.

## Files to Modify

### src/engine/window_validate.rs (lines ~1315-1326)
In apply_emit_time_policy method, add a second safelist check after the existing context-based safelist check.

## Exact Location
The apply_emit_time_policy method is at line ~1301. The existing safelist check is at lines ~1316-1326:

```rust
if self.suppress_root_finding_by_safelist(
    context_buf,
    context_base_offset,
    emitted_step_id,
    root_hint_start,
    root_hint_end,
    last_safelist_decision,
) {
    crate::perf_stats::sat_add_usize(&mut scratch.safelist_suppressed, 1);
    return None;
}
```

## Code to Add (after line 1326, before the drop_hint_end calculation)

```rust
// Also check safelist against the extracted secret bytes.
// Catches placeholder secrets (hunter2, sequential digits, base64
// example literals) even when surrounding context is innocuous.
if emitted_step_id == STEP_ROOT && self.safelist.matcher().is_match(secret_bytes) {
    crate::perf_stats::sat_add_usize(&mut scratch.safelist_suppressed, 1);
    return None;
}
```

## How to access safelist
The Engine struct has a safelist field. Check the exact type and accessor:
- Look at src/engine/core.rs for the Engine struct definition
- The safelist field is a SafelistFilter which has a matcher() method returning a &RegexSet
- RegexSet has an is_match(&[u8]) -> bool method
- Verify the exact accessor by reading the SafelistFilter impl (likely in src/engine/safelist.rs or similar)

## Pattern Compatibility
The 18 safelist patterns were designed for context windows. Most are fine on isolated secret bytes too:
- Will match secrets: hunter2 (pattern 7), 0123456789 (pattern 8), *** (pattern 3), base64 example literals (pattern 15)
- Won't match (benign no-ops): classpath:, xmlns:, template vars — these patterns simply won't fire on isolated secret bytes, which is correct

## Testing
1. Secret bytes = hunter2, clean context → suppressed (new behavior).
2. Secret bytes = 0123456789, clean context → suppressed.
3. Secret bytes = ghp_2fK9sD6nL0pQ8rT1vW3xY5zA7bC9dE1fG3hI → NOT suppressed.
4. Existing safelist_negative_examples_keep_realistic_secrets tests still pass.

## Performance
Negligible. safelist.matcher().is_match() runs a 18-pattern RegexSet on ~10-150 bytes. Only invoked on findings that passed all prior gates. Microseconds per call.

## Dependencies
None. Fully independent of all other tasks.

## Validation
cargo fmt --all && cargo check && cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings

title: Change PackExecError::Spill(String) to Spill(std::io::Error)
description:
In pack_exec.rs lines 1755 and 1775, PackExecError::Spill(String) forces a .to_string() heap allocation when a spill-file I/O operation fails. While this is an error-only path (and the alloc guard assertion runs on the success path so it won't catch this at runtime), it still performs an unnecessary heap allocation during the scan phase. The project philosophy is zero allocation after startup — even error paths should avoid allocating when possible.

Fix: Change the Spill variant from Spill(String) to Spill(std::io::Error). std::io::Error already exists from the OS layer — we just pass ownership instead of converting to String. This eliminates the .to_string() allocation entirely. PackExecError does not derive Clone, so std::io::Error (which is not Clone) is compatible.

Changes required:
1. pack_exec.rs: Change enum variant Spill(String) -> Spill(std::io::Error)
2. pack_exec.rs: Update Display impl for Spill to use write\!(f, "spill error: {err}")
3. pack_exec.rs lines 1755, 1775: Change .map_err(|err| PackExecError::Spill(err.to_string())) to .map_err(PackExecError::Spill)

Only the Spill variant needs changing — the other String-bearing variants (PackRead, Sink, ExternalBase) are constructed in setup/teardown code outside the inner decode loop.

title: Profile-Guided Optimization (PGO) pipeline
description:
## Summary

Build a Profile-Guided Optimization (PGO) pipeline for scanner-rs. Expected 5–15% overall throughput improvement based on industry benchmarks for branch-heavy interpreters. Reference existing perf data in tools/bench-compare/results/perf_analysis.md.

## Context

PGO is one of the highest-ROI optimizations for interpreter-style code like our delta chain decoder. The compiler uses runtime profiling data to:
- Optimize branch layouts (hot paths fall through, cold paths jump)
- Inline decisions based on actual call frequencies
- Better register allocation for hot loops
- Improved code placement for instruction cache locality

Our 1.91% branch miss rate and 40.67% backend stalls suggest the compiler's static heuristics aren't optimal for our actual workload distribution.

## Implementation Plan

### Phase 1: Instrumented Build
```bash
# Build with instrumentation
RUSTFLAGS="-Cprofile-generate=/tmp/pgo-data" cargo build --release
```

### Phase 2: Profile Collection
- Run the instrumented binary against representative workloads:
  - Large git repository pack parsing (e.g., linux kernel repo)
  - Delta chain decoding (deep chains, varied copy patterns)
  - Mixed object types (commits, trees, blobs of various sizes)
- Ensure profile data covers all hot paths

### Phase 3: Optimized Build
```bash
# Merge profile data
llvm-profdata merge -o /tmp/pgo-data/merged.profdata /tmp/pgo-data
# Build with profile data
RUSTFLAGS="-Cprofile-use=/tmp/pgo-data/merged.profdata" cargo build --release
```

### Phase 4: Benchmark
- Compare PGO vs non-PGO builds on the full benchmark suite
- Document per-benchmark improvements
- Pay special attention to delta chain decoding benchmarks

### Phase 5: CI Integration
- Add a Makefile target or script (e.g., `scripts/build-pgo.sh`) for reproducible PGO builds
- Document the profile collection workload so it can be refreshed when hot paths change
- Consider adding PGO to release builds in CI

## Technical Notes

- PGO requires LLVM (rustc's default backend) — no extra dependencies
- Profile data is architecture-specific: collect on the target architecture (aarch64 for Graviton3 deployment)
- BOLT (Binary Optimization and Layout Tool) is a potential follow-up for additional 5-10% on top of PGO, but is more complex to set up
- PGO profiles should be refreshed when major code changes affect hot paths

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] PGO build script exists and is documented
- [ ] Profile collection workload is defined and reproducible
- [ ] Before/after benchmark comparison documented (expect 5-15% improvement)
- [ ] CI integration plan documented (even if not yet automated)
- [ ] `cargo test` passes with PGO-optimized build

title: False sharing risk: 38 consecutive AtomicU64 counters in perf.rs

Option 3 is preferred as it also reduces atomic contention.

title: Epic: Data Layout Optimization for Scanner Throughput
description:
Optimize data layout across hot-path structures to improve cache locality, reduce working set size, and increase scanning throughput.

## Motivation
Profiling and analysis show significant cache-line waste from:
1. RuleCompiled storing large optional gate structs inline (~850+ bytes per rule even when most gates are None)
2. ScratchVec carrying a 16-byte Layout field per instance (11 instances = 440 bytes of metadata overhead)
3. StepArena storing full DecodeStep enums (32 bytes) when hot path only needs StepId (4 bytes)
4. PackedPatterns using Vec (ptr+len+cap) when Box<[T]> (ptr+len) suffices for immutable data
5. ScanScratch mixing hot and cold fields without alignment boundaries

## Design Phases
- **Phase 1 (High-confidence)**: Pool rule gates, shrink ScratchVec, compact StepArena, boxed slices
- **Phase 2 (Aggressive)**: Hot/cold ScanScratch split, lazy allocation, AoS Vectorscan metadata, u32 ScratchVec headers

## Success Criteria
- Lower cycles/byte in tier2/tier3 benchmarks
- Lower L1D miss rate under perf stat
- No semantic regressions (property tests, materialization equivalence)
- Size guard assertions for all refactored types
close_reason: All planned Phase 1 and Phase 2 data layout tasks completed; Phase 2 benchmark validation documented and changes retained. Follow-up optimization tracked in scratch-scanner-rs-ci9.

title: Compact StepArena nodes with deferred DecodeStep materialization
description:
Store a compact StepNode representation in the arena, materialize full DecodeStep only on the cold output path.

## Problem
StepNode stores parent: StepId (4 bytes) + step: DecodeStep (32 bytes) = ~40 bytes per node. But the hot path only uses StepId (4 bytes) — the full DecodeStep data is only needed when materializing findings for output.

## Solution
Replace StepNode with a compact representation:
```rust
#[repr(C)]
pub struct StepNodeCompact {
    parent: u32,          // StepId.0
    kind: u8,             // 0=Transform, 1=Utf16Le, 2=Utf16Be
    _pad: u8,
    transform_idx: u16,   // only for Transform; 0 otherwise
    span_lo: u32,
    span_hi: u32,
}
// Total: 16 bytes (down from ~40)
```

Add materialize() that reconstructs DecodeStep from compact form:
```rust
fn materialize(&self) -> DecodeStep {
    match self.kind {
        0 => DecodeStep::Transform {
            transform_idx: self.transform_idx as usize,
            parent_span: self.span_lo as usize..self.span_hi as usize,
        },
        1 => DecodeStep::Utf16Window {
            endianness: Utf16Endianness::Le,
            parent_span: self.span_lo as usize..self.span_hi as usize,
        },
        2 => DecodeStep::Utf16Window {
            endianness: Utf16Endianness::Be,
            parent_span: self.span_lo as usize..self.span_hi as usize,
        },
        _ => unreachable!(),
    }
}
```

## Correctness constraints
- Ensure transform_idx <= u16::MAX at engine build time (add assertion)
- Ensure spans fit in u32 (already true — the engine uses SpanU32 and EncRef with u32 throughout)
- Add size guard: StepNodeCompact must be exactly 16 bytes
- Unit test: build step chain with transform + utf16, verify materialize() yields identical DecodeSteps

## Impact
- ~60% reduction in arena footprint (40→16 bytes per node)
- Better cache behavior in transform-heavy scans

## Files to modify
- src/engine/decode_state.rs — replace StepNode, update push/materialize
- src/engine/core.rs — update materialization call site (line ~1567-1581)
- src/api.rs — no change needed (DecodeStep enum stays as public API)
close_reason: Compact StepNode from 40 to 16 bytes via CompactDecodeStep

description:
## Context

With suppressors compiled into `PackedPatterns` and pooled on `Engine` (Task 2), we need to evaluate them at runtime in `window_validate.rs` at all 4 secret_bytes emission sites.

## Goal

Insert the value suppressor gate check immediately after secret span extraction and before local context / hashing at all 4 match emission sites in `window_validate.rs`.

## Scope

**In scope:**
- Insert suppressor check at all 4 emission sites in `src/engine/window_validate.rs`:
  1. `run_rule_on_window()` — Raw variant (~line 455)
  2. `run_rule_on_utf16_window_aligned()` — UTF-16 decoded (~line 695)
  3. `run_rule_on_raw_window_into()` — Raw scheduler adapter (~line 851)
  4. `run_rule_on_utf16_window_aligned_into()` — UTF-16 scheduler adapter (~line 1061)
- Use existing `contains_any_memmem(secret_bytes, vs)` from `src/engine/helpers.rs`
- Unit tests for suppression behavior

**Out of scope:**
- Performance benchmarks (Task 5)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Suppressor check inserted at all 4 emission sites, after secret extraction, before local context
- [ ] When suppressor matches: finding is NOT emitted (return from closure)
- [ ] When suppressor does not match: finding IS emitted (pass-through)
- [ ] When no suppressors configured: no change in behavior (gate skipped)
- [ ] Unit test: rule with suppressor matching extracted secret → no finding
- [ ] Unit test: rule with suppressor NOT matching extracted secret → finding emitted
- [ ] Unit test: rule with multiple suppressors → any hit suppresses
- [ ] Unit test: rule without suppressors → finding emitted (regression guard)

## Technical Direction

- At each site, immediately after `let secret_bytes = &window[secret_start..secret_end];` (or decoded equivalent), add:
  ```rust
  if let Some(vs) = self.value_suppressor_gate(rule.value_suppressors) {
      if contains_any_memmem(secret_bytes, vs) {
          return; // suppress — return from closure body, not outer fn
      }
  }
  ```
- `self` here is the `Engine` reference available in the method
- The `return` is from the `for_each_capture_match` closure body — this skips emission for that match only
- All 4 sites follow the same pattern; keep the check identical at each
- Import `contains_any_memmem` if not already in scope at each site
close_reason: Implemented runtime value suppressor gate at all 4 emission sites with behavior tests.

title: Add --transforms CLI flag for per-transform-type control
description:
## Context

The scanner currently runs URL-percent and Base64 transform decoding on every chunk automatically. This is correct for general-purpose scanning — secrets can be hidden inside encoded layers. However, profiling shows transforms account for the majority of CPU time on the zero-hit path: **533 MiB/s** with transforms vs **4,490 MiB/s** without (8.4x gap). Users scanning known-plaintext corpora (e.g., source code repos with no encoded secrets) pay this cost for zero benefit.

## Goal

Let users selectively disable URL-percent and/or Base64 transform decoding via CLI flags, defaulting to all-enabled (current behavior).

## Scope

**In scope:**

* A `--transforms` CLI flag accepting a comma-separated list: `all` (default), `none`, `url`, `base64`, `url,base64`
* Wire the flag through `FsScanConfig` and `GitSourceConfig` → `build_engine()` → `demo_transforms()` filtering
* When a transform is disabled, its `TransformConfig` is excluded from the transforms vec entirely (not just `TransformMode::Disabled`) — zero overhead
* Log a warning to stderr when transforms are disabled: "Transform decoding disabled — encoded secrets will not be detected"

**Out of scope:**

* Per-rule transform overrides
* Runtime transform switching (mid-scan)
* UTF-16 variant toggling (separate concern, already has `scan_utf16_variants` in `Tuning`)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `--transforms=none` achieves throughput within 10% of the empty-transforms ceiling (~4,490 MiB/s baseline)
- [ ] `--transforms=url` disables only Base64; `--transforms=base64` disables only URL-percent
- [ ] Default behavior (no flag) is identical to current behavior — all transforms enabled
- [ ] All existing tests pass when flag is absent
- [ ] Warning printed to stderr when any transform is disabled

## Technical Direction

* **Approach:** Filter `demo_transforms()` output based on a `TransformPolicy` enum/set before passing to `Engine::new`. No engine-internal changes needed.
* Add `transforms: Option<TransformPolicy>` field to both `FsScanConfig` and `GitSourceConfig`
* `TransformPolicy` can be a simple enum: `All`, `None`, `Only(HashSet<TransformId>)` — or just a pair of bools (`enable_url_percent`, `enable_base64`)
* Wire through `build_engine()` and `run_git()` — both paths already accept transforms as a parameter
* The existing `TransformMode::Disabled` mechanism is unnecessary here since we can just exclude the config entirely from the vec
* **CLI parsing:** `clap` value parser with comma-separated values mapping to the policy

## References

* `src/demo.rs:61-87` — `demo_transforms()` returns the hardcoded transform list
* `src/unified/mod.rs:60-74` — `FsScanConfig` struct
* `src/unified/orchestrator.rs:498-502` — `build_engine()` wiring
* `src/api.rs:75-77` — `TransformId` enum (two variants: `UrlPercent`, `Base64`)
* Performance data: all-transforms=533 MiB/s, no-transforms=4,490 MiB/s, url-gate-only=655 MiB/s
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `--transforms=none` achieves throughput within 10% of the empty-transforms ceiling (~4,490 MiB/s baseline)
- [ ] `--transforms=url` disables only Base64; `--transforms=base64` disables only URL-percent
- [ ] Default behavior (no flag) is identical to current behavior — all transforms enabled
- [ ] All existing tests pass when flag is absent
- [ ] Warning printed to stderr when any transform is disabled
close_reason: Implemented: TransformFilter enum, --transforms=all|none|<list> CLI flag in both fs/git subcommands, apply_transform_filter in orchestrator, unit tests, clippy clean

title: Fix VectorscanCounters false sharing with per-worker counters
description:
Address potential false sharing in VectorscanCounters where 11 adjacent AtomicU64 fields can share cache lines.

## Problem
VectorscanCounters in src/engine/core.rs has 11 adjacent AtomicU64 fields (88 bytes) with no explicit alignment. Multiple threads incrementing different atomics can cause false-sharing on the same cache line. While Relaxed ordering mitigates synchronization cost, the cache-line bouncing remains.

## Solution options

### Option A (best): Per-worker counters with merge
```rust
struct VectorscanCountersLocal {
    scans_attempted: u64,
    scans_ok: u64,
    scans_err: u64,
    // ... non-atomic, per-worker
}
// Merge at end of scan batch
```
- Eliminates atomics entirely in hot path
- Follows existing WorkerMetricsLocal pattern

### Option B: Pad each atomic
```rust
struct VectorscanCounters {
    scans_attempted: CachePadded<AtomicU64>,
    // ... each padded to 64 bytes
}
```
- Simple but wastes memory (11 × 64 = 704 bytes vs 88 bytes)

## Recommendation
Option A is preferred — it follows the existing WorkerMetricsLocal pattern and avoids atomics in the hot path entirely.

## Files to modify
- src/engine/core.rs — refactor VectorscanCounters
- Merge logic at scan completion

## Phase 2 — only if stats feature is used during perf benchmarking. If stats is debug-only, deprioritize.
notes: Implemented false-sharing mitigation via cache-line padded atomics: introduced #[repr(align(64))] CachePaddedAtomicU64 and switched VectorscanCounters fields to padded counters. This isolates frequently updated counters to separate cache lines while preserving existing stats API and call sites.
close_reason: Mitigated Vectorscan stats false sharing with cache-line padded counters

title: UB risk: from_raw_parts_mut over uninitialized spare capacity in pack_inflate.rs

Fix: use MaybeUninit::slice_assume_init_mut or write via raw pointer (ptr::copy_nonoverlapping) instead of forming a &mut [u8] reference. title: YAML rules loading with deterministic ordering and VsDbCache reuse
description:
## Context
Today all rules are compiled into the binary via `gitleaks_rules()` in `src/gitleaks_rules.rs`. This makes rule iteration slow (recompile the whole binary) and prevents users from customizing their rule set. The Vectorscan DB disk cache (`VsDbCache`) already handles cache-key-based reuse of compiled `.hsdb` files, and `policy_hash` already canonically encodes rules for git scan caching.

## Goal
Load rules from an external YAML file at startup, replacing the compiled-in rule set, while reusing existing `VsDbCache` and `policy_hash` infrastructure for deterministic caching.

## Scope
**In scope:**
- Add `--rules=<file>` flag to both `scan fs` and `scan git`
- YAML schema mirrors `RuleSpec` fields (name, anchors, radius, regex as pattern string, etc.)
- Parse YAML into `Vec<RuleSpec>` at startup
- Ship a `default_rules.yaml` sibling file (equivalent to today's `gitleaks_rules()`)
- When `--rules` is not specified, load `default_rules.yaml` from next to the binary
- Remove compiled-in `gitleaks_rules()` — all rules are external
- Reuse existing `VsDbCache` (cache keys already derived from patterns/flags/IDs)
- Reuse existing `policy_hash` (already order-invariant for rules)

**Out of scope:**
- Directory scanning / multi-file rules
- Rule merging or overlaying
- Compiled rule packs
- Rule validation beyond what `RuleSpec::assert_valid()` already does
- Hot-reload of rules

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Running the same scan twice with the same YAML rules reuses cached `*.hsdb` files (no recompilation)
- [ ] Changing a YAML rule's regex or anchors produces new cache keys and new `*.hsdb` files
- [ ] Rule ordering is stable across runs (single-file array index)
- [ ] `policy_hash` changes when scanning-relevant rule fields change (because `RuleSpec::encode_policy` includes them)
- [ ] `--rules=<file>` works for both `scan fs` and `scan git`
- [ ] When `--rules` is omitted, `default_rules.yaml` is loaded from the binary's sibling directory
- [ ] Clear error message if the rules file is missing or malformed

## Technical Direction
- **Serde**: Add `serde::Deserialize` to a `YamlRuleSpec` struct with string-typed fields, then convert to `RuleSpec` (compile regex, parse anchors from strings to `&'static [u8]` via leaking or an arena)
- **Anchor encoding**: Anchors as hex strings or UTF-8 strings in YAML, converted to `&'static [u8]` at load time
- **Static lifetime**: Since rules live for the program's duration, `Box::leak` the parsed strings/vecs to produce `&'static` references matching `RuleSpec`'s current lifetime requirements
- **Default file location**: `std::env::current_exe()` → parent dir → join `default_rules.yaml`
- **CLI parsing**: Add `--rules=<path>` to the hand-rolled parser in `src/unified/cli.rs`, threaded into both `FsArgs` and `GitArgs`
- **Existing cache/hash untouched**: `VsDbCache` and `policy_hash` already work generically over `&[RuleSpec]` — no changes needed there

## References
- `src/api.rs:581` — `RuleSpec` definition
- `src/engine/vs_cache.rs` — `VsDbCache` cache key and storage
- `src/git_scan/policy_hash.rs` — `policy_hash()` with order-invariant rule encoding
- `src/unified/cli.rs` — hand-rolled CLI parser
- `src/gitleaks_rules.rs` — current compiled-in rules (to be converted to YAML)
- `src/demo.rs:57` — `demo_rules()` entry point
close_reason: Implemented: YAML rules loading with --rules= CLI flag, default_rules.yaml generation (223 rules), fallback chain (explicit > default_rules.yaml > compiled-in), round-trip test. All 932 lib + 122 integration + 2 smoke tests pass.

title: Split ScanScratch into hot/cold regions with alignment boundaries
description:
Separate ScanScratch into hot and cold nested structs with explicit cache-line alignment between them.

## Problem
ScanScratch has 47 fields mixing hot scan-loop fields with cold/conditional fields. Hot metadata (hit_acc_pool, touched_pairs, windows, out) shares cache lines with cold fields (decode_ring, pending wheels, base64_stats) causing unnecessary cache pollution.

## Solution (Approach A — low risk)
```rust
pub struct ScanScratch {
    hot: ScanScratchHot,   // out, work_q, hit_acc_pool, touched_pairs, windows, expanded, spans, seen_findings_scan
    #[repr(align(64))]
    cold: ScanScratchCold, // decode_ring, pending_windows, stream state, base64_stats, entropy_scratch
}
```

This doesn't change ownership or lifetimes — just improves packing and prevents hot/cold cache-line sharing.

## Categorization
**Hot** (scan loop critical):
- out, norm_hash, drop_hint_end, work_q, work_head
- hit_acc_pool, touched_pairs, windows, expanded, spans
- seen_findings_scan, max_findings, findings_dropped

**Cold** (conditional/streaming):
- decode_ring, window_bytes, vs_stream_matches
- pending_spans, span_streams, pending_windows
- tmp_findings, tmp_drop_hint_end, tmp_norm_hash
- entropy_scratch (1284 bytes\!), base64_stats
- slab, seen, seen_findings, root_span_map_ctx
- All VsScratch options

## Files to modify
- src/engine/scratch.rs — restructure into nested structs
- All files that access ScanScratch fields — update field paths (scratch.hot.X / scratch.cold.X)

## Phase 2 — only pursue after Phase 1 benchmarks show remaining cache pressure
notes: Implemented hot/cold ScanScratch layout split with a 64-byte alignment boundary marker and #[repr(C)] field-order guarantee; updated docs/memory-management.md and added layout regression test scanscratch_cold_region_is_cacheline_aligned.
close_reason: Implemented and validated hot/cold ScanScratch cache-line boundary split

title: Add --event-format=text|json|sarif output styles via new EventSink implementations
description:
## Context
The unified CLI emits structured scan events via the `EventSink` trait (`src/unified/events.rs`), with `JsonlEventSink` as the only format. CI integrations need SARIF for GitHub Code Scanning, JSON for programmatic consumption, and human-readable text for terminal use. The architecture already supports this — `EventFormat` enum, `EventEncoder` trait, and `build_event_sink()` factory are all extension points.

## Goal
Add `--event-format=text|json|sarif` output styles as new `EventSink` implementations, keeping scanning hot paths completely unchanged.

## Scope
**In scope:**
- Extend `EventFormat` enum with `Text`, `Json`, `Sarif` variants
- Implement `TextEventSink` — compact one-liner by default, multi-line with `--verbose`
- Implement `JsonEventSink` — streaming JSON array document
- Implement `SarifEventSink` — SARIF 2.1.0 with byteOffset-based regions
- Factor JSON escaping helpers into a reusable `json_write` module (shared by JSONL/JSON/SARIF)
- Optimize `JsonlEventSink` to use thread-local buffer reuse instead of per-emit `Vec` allocation
- Wire new formats into `parse_event_format()` and `build_event_sink()`

**Out of scope:**
- `--output=<path>` file output (follow-up story)
- Fingerprints, grouping/dedup across files/commits
- Line/column/snippet enrichment
- Web UI viewer

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `scanner-rs scan fs --path <dir> --event-format=text` prints one-liner findings to stdout
- [ ] `--event-format=text --verbose` prints multi-line finding blocks
- [ ] `--event-format=json` outputs valid JSON array parseable by `serde_json::from_slice`
- [ ] `--event-format=sarif` outputs valid SARIF 2.1.0 JSON with required envelope keys (`version`, `$schema`, `runs`) and one result per finding
- [ ] No interleaving/corruption under multi-threaded emission (unit test: spawn N threads, emit M events, validate output)
- [ ] Existing `--event-format=jsonl` output unchanged (default)
- [ ] JSONL per-emit allocation reduced via thread-local buffer reuse

## Technical Direction
- **Pattern**: Mirror `JsonlEventSink` structure — `Mutex<BufWriter<W>>`, format outside lock, `write_all()` inside lock
- **JSON sink**: Write `[` on construction, `,\n` between results (track `first: AtomicBool`), `]` on `flush()`
- **SARIF sink**: Same streaming pattern as JSON sink but emit SARIF envelope. On `flush()`, close the `results` array and `runs`/root braces
- **Text sink compact**: `{path}:{start}-{end}  {rule_name}  ({source})` — one line per finding, summary/progress events as-is
- **Text sink verbose**: Multi-line block with labeled fields (rule, path, range, source, commit if present)
- **JSON escaping module**: Extract `write_json_str`, `write_json_bytes`, `write_u64`, `write_f64` from `JsonlEncoder` into `src/unified/json_write.rs`. All sinks import from there.
- **Thread-local buffer**: Use `std::cell::RefCell<Vec<u8>>` in a `thread_local!` macro for `JsonlEventSink::emit()` to reuse allocation across calls
- **SARIF result mapping**: `ruleId` = `rule_name`, `message.text` = `"Secret matched rule {rule_name}"`, `locations[0].physicalLocation.artifactLocation.uri` = escaped path, `region.byteOffset` = start, `region.byteLength` = end - start

## References
- `src/unified/events.rs` — EventSink trait, JsonlEventSink, JsonlEncoder
- `src/unified/mod.rs:102-108` — EventFormat enum
- `src/unified/cli.rs:342-350` — parse_event_format()
- `src/unified/orchestrator.rs:229-234` — build_event_sink()
- [SARIF 2.1.0 spec](https://docs.oasis-open.org/sarif/sarif/v2.1.0/sarif-v2.1.0.html)
close_reason: All 6 subtasks complete: json_write extraction, thread-local buffers, Text/JSON/SARIF sinks, stress tests
